scenes.head: LectureLoop
scenes.body: The forgetting curve starts the moment class ends. Turn the lecture you just heard into a 3-minute review before you leave the room.

scenes.head: Record in class
scenes.body: It keeps recording with the screen off (a microphone foreground service).

scenes.head: ...or use any recording
scenes.body: Pick the file and name the class.

scenes.head: Checked, then heard
scenes.body: The server checks the RevenueCat entitlement and the weekly allowance first, then Gemini listens and must answer in a strict JSON schema. The app re-checks every rule and retries once with the reasons.

scenes.head: Only what the lecturer said
scenes.body: Exam hints with their exact words, key ideas, and homework with the deadline as spoken. Tap a time to hear that moment.

scenes.head: The loop: day 1, 3, 7
scenes.body: Next day (clock moved forward for this demo). 4 of 5 correct moves the lecture on; a miss brings it back tomorrow.

scenes.head: 2 free lectures a week
scenes.body: The limit comes from RevenueCat offering metadata and is enforced by the server too. Semester Pass = one term. 'pro' unlocks it, and the waiting recording is built straight away. (RevenueCat Test Store)

scenes.head: Real lectures are 75 minutes
scenes.body: Long recordings are cut into 10-minute windows and heard in parallel, so every timestamp stays on the right sentence and the quiz covers the whole lecture.

scenes.head: Manage it in the app
scenes.body: RevenueCat Customer Center handles cancel and restore.

scenes.head: LectureLoop
scenes.body: Open source (MIT): github.com/Ryugi62/lectureloop. Built by a student whose desktop prototype has turned 27 of their own lectures into review pages this semester.
